summary.intent: Execute all plans for CipherBox phase 68.1 (web client runtime integration) via wave-based parallel subagent orchestration, verify the phase against its success criteria, live-test the running stack, and then plan and begin executing gap-closure fixes for issues found during verification and user manual testing.
summary.outcome: All 14 original plans executed across 5 waves (58 commits), phase verification scored 2/5 criteria met (owned/shared flows and e2e-green gaps remained), the user manually reproduced a nested-folder-creation bug and a post-logout navigation failure, root causes were diagnosed and documented in VERIFICATION.md addenda, gap-closure plans (68.1-15/16/17/18/21) were generated and are now executing in waves with fixes landing (kind-cache wiring, TEE republish enrollment, D-05 stale-record toast routing) and one fixture regression already caught and repaired mid-wave.

repo: GSD execute-phase workflow spawns one subagent per plan, groups plans into dependency-based waves, and runs post-merge build/test/drift gates after each wave before advancing

Wave subagents run in isolated git worktrees (`.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>`) and report `<worktree_metadata>` (agent_id, worktree_path, branch, expected_base) that the orchestrator must record in a wave manifest before merging

Subagent-reported `expected_base` can be wrong (an agent's own docs commit instead of the true fork point) — orchestrator must verify the true fork base via git before merging, not trust the field blindly
gap-analysis.plan-post is a non-blocking advisory gate that runs after planning artifacts are committed
Decision-coverage gate requires the `[informational]` tag to sit inside the bold ID group, e.g. `- **D-04 [informational]:**`, not appended after it, or the parser won't detect it

mock-ipns-routing (dev delegated routing) keeps IPNS records in an in-memory Map — any container restart wipes all unregistered records, causing permanent 404s for folders whose records were never persisted to the API's ipns_records DB table

createFolder previously published child IPNS records without encryptedIpnsPrivateKey/keyEpoch, so ipns_republish_schedule had zero rows — subfolder records were never enrolled for TEE republish and would die at IPNS TTL in production

The mock-ipns-routing container's healthcheck used bare `wget localhost`, which resolves to `::1`, but the app binds IPv4-only on that port — causing perpetual 'unhealthy' status unrelated to actual service health; fixed via docker-compose.yml healthcheck target

D-05 stale-record rejection toast bug: ROT-07 anti-rollback floor is bumped pre-publish, one step ahead of the client's own subsequent publish, so a relay replay from just before that publish exactly matches the floor and slips past enforceResolved as a generic ReconcileStaleError instead of triggering rejection

Migration 1750000000000-ApiSchemaCutover dropped the `shares` table's plaintext `item_name` column entirely; share.service.ts now hardcodes itemName:'', making the REQ-4 itemName backfill feature permanently dead code (documented as GAP-6, not silently patched, since reviving plaintext item names server-side would violate the project's zero-knowledge architecture)

code.finding: resolveFileMetadata's first parameter changed from bare fileIpnsName:string to full SealedChildRef, since readKeySealed/generation needed to derive a file's readKey only exist on the parent's SealedChildRef
Hardcoded isFolder = true stub meant the D-02 kind cache was never consulted in the shared browser, causing files to render/behave as folders
restoreFromBin lacked hardening for a dead restored-child IPNS record; fixed to warn (non-throwing) when a restored child's own record doesn't resolve post-relink

workflow: When a long-running background executor agent's completion signal is lost (session evicted mid-wait), spot-check filesystem/git/process state directly rather than assuming a hang, then resume the agent via SendMessage with the verified results so it can pick up where it left off

For a serial (describe.serial) Playwright suite, a failure early in setup causes the rest of that spec's tests to be skipped, not passed — raw 'N failed / M passed' tallies overstate real coverage when failures cluster in shared setup steps

Running a target spec in headed mode alongside a background triage agent risks two concurrent runs fighting over the same dev stack/screen — check for a running process before launching a headed reproduction
A subagent's self-reported git metadata (e.g. expected_base) can be inaccurate; the orchestrator should independently verify fork points before merging worktrees
When a gate that pipes through `tail` reports success, the real exit code can still be non-zero — always check the actual command exit status rather than relying on truncated output framing

friction: Wave 1 agent for plan 68.1-01 stalled mid-stream after 119 tool calls (~23 min), requiring a fallback spot-check and manual resume via SendMessage

Exit-gate agent (68.1-13) launched the 208-spec Playwright suite in the background then was never re-woken when it finished — its session was evicted, losing ~1+ hour before the orchestrator noticed and manually resumed it
git index.lock transiently blocked a tracking commit during Wave 3 close, requiring a lock/process check and retry
A subagent (68.1-16) ran a prohibited `git stash push`/attempted workaround on bin/index.ts mid-task, leaving a stray stash entry that had to be identified and dropped during wave cleanup
Decision-coverage gate initially rejected the D-04 informational tag due to placement outside the bold ID group, requiring investigation of the parser's matching logic before fixing
A Bash command requesting to view compose file port config plus .env was denied (likely the .env read), requiring the check to be split into separate calls

Wave 2 gap-closure test gate falsely appeared to pass due to a `tail`-truncated view masking a real failure (19 stale test fixtures broken by a fileReadKey/fileWriteKey contract change from plan 68.1-07/09), requiring a resumed-agent fix cycle before the wave could advance
TaskList/task tracking did not survive a session hand-off after the long e2e wait, forcing the orchestrator to proceed without it for the remaining linear steps
